ety.text: From Middle French immature. Partially displaced unripe, from Old English unrīpe (“unripe, immature”).

senses.d: An artillery fire mission modifier for two types of fire mission to denote an immediate need for fire: Immediate smoke, all guns involved must reload smoke and fire. ex: Hotel Two-Niner, this is Bravo Six. Immediate suppression at grid November-Kilo four-five-three two-one-five. Danger Close. I authenticate Golf Echo, over.

ety.text: From Middle English immunite, from Old French immunité, from Latin immūnitās, in the legal sense; for the medical use see immunization. Equivalent to immune + -ity. Displaced native Old English frēols (“privilege, immunity”).

senses.d: Protective resistance against disease.
ex: Some people have better immunity to diseases than others.

senses.d: An exemption from specified duties, such as payments or services.
ex: Feudal privileges often included tax and other immunities.

senses.d: An exemption from prosecution.
ex: The prosecutor offered the lieutenant immunity for all the crimes he would testify having known to be planned by the elusive drug baron.

senses.d: An exemption from penance.
An exemption given to a player from losing or being withdrawn from play.
ex: After winning the last round the player was granted immunity which allowed him to stay in the game even after receiving the fewest points.

senses.d: A resistance to a specific thing.
ex: Superbugs are bacteria that develop an immunity to antibiotics.
